confidence_rationale: The harm evidence is strong: Human Rights Watch (tier 5) and the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (tier 5) directly document the conduct scored. Confidence is held at medium rather than high because no independent outcome evaluation of the Tekavoul safety net was located, so the positive dimensions (Action, Equity) rest on coverage figures rather than measured effect, and two subdimensions rely on unwatch.org at tier 3.
rationale: Mauritania is published at composite 20.3 on a never-assessed uniform seed vector (2/2/2/1.5/2/1.5/2/1.5) shared byte-identically by twelve countries at ranks 134-145 of the countries index. notes: Filed under the revised band-crossing clause: a proposal may be filed when EITHER the absolute composite delta is at least 5.0 points OR the assessed band differs from the published band, at any delta. This proposal is filed on the second condition. The composite delta is -2.8 points, which would NOT have been filable under the previous 5.0-point-only rule, and the original Mauritania assessment therefore recorded "do not file" on that basis. The movement is a seed-baseline de-seeding, not a finding of new misconduct: Mauritania was published on a never-assessed uniform seed vector (2/2/2/1.5/2/1.5/2/1.5, composite 20.3) shared byte-identically by twelve countries at ranks 134-145 of the countries index. Replacing that placeholder with 40 measured subdimension scores moves the composite to 17.5, which crosses the 20.0 boundary from Developing into Critical. No subdimension score, evidence item or composite has been re-scored or altered for this filing; every value is carried verbatim from the 2026-08-16 assessment and its sidecar.
